But 'when not to use' and consequences overstate the boundary: they say a solution 'more or less general than the statement is a hard error' (applicability.avoid_when, consequences in entry.json, and README consequences). The cited mechanism does not reject a MORE general solution: P2M/Util.lean #p2m_type_eq (L19-40) only reports P2M_TYPE_MISMATCH and P2M_UNDERGENERAL ('the proof is less general than the card'), and p2m_exact_reverting (L3-16) uses elabTermEnsuringType, which specialises a more-general term to the goal. Only a mismatch or an under-general (less general) solution is the hard error. Claiming more-general is rejected wrongly steers users away from a valid, desirable case. Fix: in applicability.avoid_when and both consequences texts, replace 'more or less general' / 'more general or less general' with 'less general (under-general)', and note a more-general proof is accepted (specialised to the statement).
